title: Harder Ion Testing Question
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Describe tests to identify the anions: (a) carbonate, CO3²⁻, by reaction with dilute acid and then testing for carbon dioxide gas (b) chloride, Cl⁻, bromide, Br⁻, and iodide, I⁻, by acidifying with dilute nitric acid then adding aqueous silver nitrate (c) nitrate, NO3⁻, reduction with aluminium foil and aqueous sodium hydroxide and then testing for ammonia gas (d) sulfate, SO4²⁻, by acidifying with dilute nitric acid and then adding aqueous barium nitrate (e) sulfite, SO3²⁻, by reaction with acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII)

Describe tests using aqueous sodium hydroxide and aqueous ammonia to identify the aqueous cations: (a) aluminium, Al³⁺ (b) ammonium, NH4⁺ (c) calcium, Ca²⁺ (d) chromium(III), Cr³⁺ (e) copper(II), Cu²⁺ (f) iron(II), Fe²⁺ (g) iron(III), Fe³⁺ (h) zinc, Zn²⁺
Interpret and evaluate experimental observations and data
